newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends sharply up on frost, funds, CBOT.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends sharply up on frost, funds, CBOT.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended sharply up on frost on the northwest Prairie grainbelt Tuesday morning as well as exporter and fund buying, traders said.
"We're up on the weather concerns, StatsCan's report this morning and it's pretty hard to ignore those (CBOT) beans," a trader said.
Nov-Mar spread at $4, Sep-Nov $5, May-July $1. Funds bought more than 1,500 November late in the session. Volume was heavy at 6,485 lots, or 129,700 tonnes, with 950 hedges.
Japan bought 4,000-5,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
November canola rose $8 to $439.70, January up $7.50 to $443. October flax up $4 to $394.50 on StatsCan's report.

October feed wheat rose $3.10 to $209.30, December up $3.30 to $195.50 on commission stop loss short covering at $208 in October and $195 in December. Oct-Dec spread at $13.50 Oct-Mar $14.50, Dec-Mar $1.50, Mar-May even. Volume was heavy.
November western barley rose $1.80 to $153.80, February up $1.60 to $157.80 on commercial short covering and to keep the feed wheat-barley straddle within $40 to $42. Volume 1,175.
UGG bought December feed peas up US$0.30 to US$211.30 and selling the Oct-Dec spread to LFG at US$1, traders said. Oats didn't trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
